rows.vgi.doc_md:
# Classical NLP for DuckDB SQL

![spaCy logo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/88/SpaCy_logo.svg)

Run **classical natural language processing in SQL** -- language detection, sentiment analysis, named entity recognition (NER), lemmatization, and tokenization -- directly over your text columns in DuckDB, with no LLM and no API key required. This worker turns the proven open-source NLP stack of [spaCy](https://spacy.io), [fastText](https://fasttext.cc/), and [VADER](https://github.com/cjhutto/vaderSentiment) into fast, deterministic SQL functions for bulk, cheap, per-row text enrichment.

## Who it is for

Data engineers and analysts who want to enrich large text tables -- product reviews, support tickets, articles, social posts -- without leaving SQL or paying per token. Because the underlying models are rule- and statistics-based rather than generative, output is reproducible and runs at column scale -- ideal *upstream* of, not as a replacement for, LLM workers.

## Key concepts

- **Models load once per worker process and are cached**, so the one-time model-load cost is amortized across every row of every query.
- **Language identification** uses Facebook's [fastText lid.176](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html) model (176 languages). When you do not pin a language, each row is routed to the matching language pipeline automatically.
- **Sentiment** uses the lexicon-and-rule-based VADER scorer, tuned for English and social media text; it understands negation, intensifiers, and emoji.
- **Linguistic analysis** -- structured span extraction, part-of-speech tagging, sentence boundaries, noun-phrase mining, lemmatization, and Unicode normalization -- uses spaCy's small English pipeline (`en_core_web_sm`) by default; pin a language or name a specific model to override it.

## When to reach for it

Use it whenever you need to enrich or filter free text at scale in SQL: detect and segment multilingual corpora, score or bucket opinion, clean and canonicalize text so free-text keys join and group reliably, or split documents into structured rows you can aggregate and join back to their source. Attach the worker, then call the functions directly from SQL -- `nlp.main.detect_lang(body)`, `nlp.main.sentiment(body)`, or `nlp.main.entities((SELECT id, body FROM docs), id := 'id')`:

```sql
INSTALL vgi FROM community;
LOAD vgi;
ATTACH 'nlp' (TYPE vgi, LOCATION 'uv run nlp_worker.py');
```

Powered by spaCy ([source](https://github.com/explosion/spaCy) - [docs](https://spacy.io/usage)), fastText ([source](https://github.com/facebookresearch/fastText) - [docs](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html)), and VADER ([source & docs](https://github.com/cjhutto/vaderSentiment)). Source for this worker: [Query-farm/vgi-nlp](https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-nlp).
